subject.title: feat(mxc): add Windows MXC sandbox backend

question: Should OpenClaw accept this first-party external MXC sandbox plugin with `@microsoft/mxc-sdk@0.7.0`, `node-pty` build allowance, and the SDK's argv-carried base64 config transport after the stray SDK export is removed?
rationale: Automation can remove the leftover export, but approving a native Windows sandbox dependency graph and a preview SDK transport boundary is a maintainer/security judgment.

options.title: Approve after export removal
options.body: Remove the unnecessary public sandbox export, then approve the exact-head dependency graph and documented MXC SDK argv transport for this prerelease plugin.

options.title: Pause for upstream transport
options.body: Keep the PR open but require an upstream MXC SDK transport that does not carry the encoded config on argv before merging.

options.title: External incubation only
options.body: Do not make MXC first-party yet; ask for independent plugin incubation until the MXC SDK and dependency boundary are mature enough.

recommendation.title: Approve after export removal
recommendation.body: Remove the unnecessary public sandbox export, then approve the exact-head dependency graph and documented MXC SDK argv transport for this prerelease plugin.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the current assignee and the recent current-main contributor on the central sandbox/plugin packaging surfaces, making them the best visible owner to route the remaining maintainer/security decision.
